title: the Bell House Rising
premise: Isandro Oyelaran takes a teaching post in the fog-bound town of Bell Hollow, where a classroom of students vanished decades ago and the school's founders left an unfinished protective ritual. When her late grandmother's house begins rearranging itself—extra chairs appearing in old photographs, doors that must be counted each night—Isandro learns she has inherited the role of Keeper, the one person who can complete the founders' ritual before the winter frost seals the boundary between the living town and the taken. Torn between the duty she never asked for and her growing love for Mara, a local archivist whose own family was among the missing, Isandro discovers the vanished class never left at all. In the climax, she chooses to finish the ritual not by sealing the door but by opening it, naming the missing aloud and letting them go, at the cost of her own place in the town's memory. The book ends with the frost receding, the photographs restored to their true count, and Isandro leaving Bell Hollow—remembered only by Mara, who keeps one extra chair by the window in case she returns.
about_author: Paloma Okonkwo is the pen name of a Nigerian-British writer who grew up between Lagos and a rain-lashed coastal town in Cornwall, a duality that haunts her fiction. She writes horror about houses that remember, drawing on her years as a schoolteacher and her family's stories of inheritances that arrive with instructions.

chapters.title: The Counting House
chapters.summary: Isandro arrives in Bell Hollow to teach at Bell House School, where the caretaker, Mr. Voss, teaches her the nightly ritual: count the doors, keep the lights on. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking her grief over her grandmother's recent death.

chapters.title: Twenty-Three Desks
chapters.summary: Isandro's class roster lists twenty-two students, but twenty-three desks are always occupied by morning, and no one claims the extra. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: the first crack in her rationalism, sharpened by the students' practiced silence about it.

chapters.title: What the Frost Draws
chapters.summary: Frost patterns on the classroom windows form legible names each dawn—names of children absent from every record. POV Mara, the town archivist, who has been quietly collecting the same names for years. Emotional beat: recognition between two women who both refuse to look away.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Sorting her grandmother's belongings, Isandro finds family photographs in which an empty chair appears in rooms where no chair stood, growing closer to the camera in each successive decade. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: dread braided with tenderness, as if her grandmother left her a warning in pictures.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: Isandro presses the headmaster about the class that vanished in 1968; he gives her a sealed founders' ledger and a warning to stop counting. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: institutional gaslighting that hardens her resolve into something like anger.

chapters.title: Mara's Archive
chapters.summary: Mara shows Isandro the archive's hidden shelf: yearbooks with faces scratched out, a register where an entire form was ruled through in red. POV Mara. Emotional beat: the intimacy of shared obsession, and the first unspoken pull between them.

chapters.title: Doors at Night
chapters.summary: The house begins moving at night—doors appearing where walls were, the count changing. Isandro keeps the lights on and answers a knock with her grandmother's voice behind it. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: terror laced with longing, because grief is the house's favorite key.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro breaks the ledger's seal: the founders didn't build the school to educate but to contain, and their ritual was left deliberately unfinished, passed Keeper to Keeper. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: the vertigo of inheritance—she was chosen before she was born.

chapters.title: What Voss Counts
chapters.summary: Isandro follows Voss on his rounds and sees him counting doors that aren't there, whispering names; he confesses he was the last Keeper's assistant and has been holding the ritual together alone for forty years. POV Voss. Emotional beat: exhausted devotion, and relief at finally handing the weight on.

chapters.title: The Taken Class
chapters.summary: In the archive's sealed sub-basement, Isandro and Mara find the 1968 classroom preserved mid-lesson, chalk dust unmoved, twenty-three desks occupied by children who do not age. POV Mara. Emotional beat: horror and heartbreak fused—her uncle is among them, still eight years old.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: The house tests Isandro: it offers her a room where her grandmother still lives, warm and real, if she abandons the ritual. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: the cruelest temptation—belonging offered as a bribe—and her refusal costs her something she can't name yet.

chapters.title: Love Against the Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara and Isandro admit what's growing between them the same night the frost writes Mara's name on the school windows. POV Mara. Emotional beat: love declared under a deadline, tender and furious at once.

chapters.title: The Ritual, Unfinished
chapters.summary: Deciphering the ledger, they learn the ritual requires the Keeper to name every taken soul aloud at the winter boundary—but the founders stopped at twenty names, fearing what naming the last three would release. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: dread of the gap in the list, and the dawning question of who the last three are.

chapters.title: The Founders' Children
chapters.summary: Mara uncovers that the final three names belong to the founders' own children, taken as the ritual's price, and that the founders fled rather than speak them. POV Mara. Emotional beat: the inheritance theme turned rotten—what parents will sacrifice, and what they'll run from.

chapters.title: Frost Writes Its Pattern
chapters.summary: The frost completes a map of the town across every surface in Bell Hollow, and the taken children begin appearing at windows all over town, waiting. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: the whole town's complicity exposed—everyone always knew, everyone always looked away.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot
chapters.summary: Confronting the town council, Isandro finds the elders are the founders' descendants, keeping the ritual broken so the past stays buried and their names stay clean. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: righteous fury; she chooses the missing over the living who abandoned them.

chapters.title: What Voss Owes
chapters.summary: Voss reveals the ritual's true cost: the Keeper who completes it will be unmade from the town's memory, a final chair emptied. He offers to take her place; she refuses. POV Voss. Emotional beat: sacrifice refused, duty and love colliding head-on.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: On the winter solstice, Isandro enters the preserved classroom as the frost closes in, and the house offers its final bargain: stay, and belong forever among the taken. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: the blurb's promise fulfilled—staying invisible was never an option; now neither is staying at all.

chapters.title: Twenty-Three Names
chapters.summary: The climax: at the boundary's thinnest hour, Isandro speaks all twenty-three names, including the founders' children, and the classroom exhales. The children age a year in a breath and step through the opened door into whatever comes next. POV Isandro. Emotional beat: grief and release in the same act—love expressed not as keeping but as letting go.

chapters.title: The Emptying House
chapters.summary: The ritual completes; Bell House goes dark and still, its extra doors gone, its frost plain glass. Isandro begins to fade from the town's memory as the price takes hold. POV Mara. Emotional beat: watching someone you love dissolve from the world while she still stands in front of you.

chapters.title: One Chair by the Window
chapters.summary: Spring. The photographs are corrected, the class of 1968 mourned and remembered, the town reckoning with what it buried. Mara sets a single extra chair by her window and writes Isandro's name in the archive where no frost can reach it. POV Mara. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into keeping—memory as an act of love.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Months later, a new teacher arrives at another school in another fog-bound town and finds a note in her desk in Isandro's handwriting: count the doors, keep the lights on, and when they offer you belonging, ask what it costs. POV the new teacher, with Isandro's voice threading through. Emotional beat: the inheritance continues—duty passed hand to hand, love outlasting the forgetting, and the quiet promise that Isandro is still out there, rising.
